The Honourable Sri Justice A.Santhosh Reddy
 S.A.Nos.1422 & 1609 Of 2011
Common Judgment

:
As these second appeals arise out of A.S.No.61 of 2010 and in between the same parties, they are being heard together and disposed of by this common judgment.
2. S.A.No.1422 of 2011 is directed against the judgment and decree dated 18.08.2011 in A.S.No.61 of 2010, on the file of the I-Additional District Judge, Karimnagar, wherein the said appeal filed by the respondent No.1 herein (plaintiff) was allowed with costs Rs.20,000/- by setting aside the judgment and decree dated 02.12.2010 in O.S.No.93 of 2009, on the file of the Senior Civil Judge, Sircilla,
whereunder the suit filed by respondent No.1 herein (plaintiff) was dismissed.
The appellate Court also imposed costs of Rs.25,000/- on respondent No.2 herein (defendant No.2).
S.A.No.1609 of 2011 is filed by defendant No.2 challenging the judgment and decree of the appellate Court.
3. For the sake of convenience, the parties are hereinafter referred to as arrayed in the suit.

4. Heard Sri M.Jagannatha Sarma, Sri Gopala Krishna Kalanidhi, Smt. Annapurna Reddy, learned counsel appearing for the parties.
5.

The averments of the plaint, in brief, are as follows:
The plaintiff, working as Manager in A.P., Cooperative Fabrics, Mancherial of Adilabad District, took an amount of Rs.8,200/- as hand loan from defendant No.1,
who is his close relative, on 18.07.1983 to meet his personal expenses, by keeping the original sale deed in respect of an open house plot situated in Karimnagar Town,
towards collateral security.

According to the plaintiff, after 24 years, defendant No.1 suddenly approached defendant No.2 (S.I of Police, Karimnagar II Town P.S) and gave a false complaint stating that the plaintiff had cheated him by not registering sale deed in his favour and the same registered as a case in Cr.No.5 of 2007 for the offence punishable under Section 420 IPC and later sent a constable to bring the plaintiff to police station on 09.01.2007 at 03:00 p.m.

entities.text: S.I of Police, Karimnagar II Town
entities.label: RESPONDENT

sentences.text: Subsequently, the plaintiff was forced to undergo illegal confinement till 12.01.2007 evening.
Meanwhile, due to coercion and threats by defendant No.2, the plaintiff was forced to execute sale deed in respect of suit schedule property in favour of defendant No.1.
Defendant No.2 threatened the plaintiff by saying that, if he failed to execute sale deed, he would be arrested and sent to judicial custody.

Since 13th, 14th and 15th of January, 2007 happened to be holidays owing to Sankranti festival and as the court would be closed,
the plaintiff had to spend three days in jail. Defendant No.2 warned the plaintiff that as he is a government employee, he would be suspended from service for spending more than 48 hours in jail.

Accordingly, the plaintiff under threat and coercion and in T. Srinivasa Rao vs Cherala Satyanarayana on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161569058/
1 order to save his job, found no way except to register sale deed on the force of defendant No.2.
6.

sentences.text: According to the plaintiff, he, having executed sale deed on 12.01.2007 in favour of defendant No.1, was allowed to go to his house.
The police have shown the plaintiff in case papers as if he was absconding.

On 17.01.2007, the plaintiff approached the Superintendent of Police, Karimnagar and submitted a representation and later he filed anticipatory bail application before the III Additional District Judge, Karimnagar and the same was allowed and he was granted bail.

The plaintiff made another representation to the S.P, Karimnagar to close Cr.No.5 of 2007 as the III-Additional District Judge, Karimnagar observed that the contents of the F.I.R., show the case as civil in nature.

According to the plaintiff, defendant No.1 failed to recover the amount of Rs.8,200/- from the plaintiff by filing a suit or filing a suit for specific performance and to overcome the limitation aspect, defendant No.1 approached the police after 24 years with false allegations and got registered a crime and later with coercion, got registered sale deed by him.
7.
It is further pleaded that defendant No.1 started construction of house in the suit schedule property without obtaining any permission from the municipality.

Defendant No.2 by misusing his official capacity confined the plaintiff for more than 70 hours and got registered sale deed with him under force and coercion and defendant No.2 is also liable to be sued.

Therefore, the plaintiff prayed to declare the sale deed executed by him in favour of defendant No.1 as cancelled and to restrain defendant No.1 from raising any construction over the suit land, besides directing defendant Nos.2 and 3 to pay damages of Rs.1 lakh.
8.
Defendant Nos.1 and 2 filed separate written statements and defendant No.3 adopted the written statement of defendant No.2.
Defendant No.1 denied all the material allegations of the plaint.

It is further stated by defendant No.1 that the plaintiff, having received sale consideration or Rs.8,200/-
from him voluntarily, executed a simple sale deed in his favour on 18.07.1983 and delivered possession of the suit property and also gave his original sale deed dated 25.01.1974 relating to the schedule property to him and since then he has been in possession and enjoyment of the same.
Subsequently, when defendant No.1 wanted to proceed with the construction of the house in the suit vacant site by obtaining loan, he was informed that simple sale deed is not sufficient and he should get a registered sale deed.
Later, he approached the plaintiff and requested him to execute registered sale deed in his favour, but the plaintiff refused for the same and demanded some more amount from him.
Later, defendant No.1 lodged a complaint before defendant No.2, who registered as case in Cr.No.5 of 2007 under Section 420 IPC against the plaintiff.

Subsequently, the plaintiff wanted to settle the matter unequivocally in order to escape from criminal prosecution and voluntarily agreed to execute a registered sale deed in his favour by receiving a sum of Rs.2,73,000/- and accordingly,
the plaintiff executed a registered sale deed dated 12.01.2007 in favour of defendant No.1.
The plaintiff on the instigation of his friends created a false story of force and coercion to gain wrongfully and grab the suit property.
According to defendant No.1, he constructed the house in the suit property long back and house No.9-5-425/1 was also allotted.
The plaintiff has no right over the suit property and the suit is not maintainable under law and is liable to be dismissed.

sentences.text: Defendant No.2 denied all the contents of plaint stating that he did not confine the plaintiff illegally as alleged in the plaint and that he is not liable for any damages as prayed by the plaintiff.
Defendant No.2 prayed for dismissal of the suit.

10. On the strength of the above pleadings, the trial Court framed the following issues:
i. Whether the plaintiff is entitled for cancellation of the registered sale deed under document No.393/07, dated 12.01.2007?
ii. Whether the plaintiff is entitled for an injunction as prayed for?
iii. Whether the plaintiff is entitled for damages from D-1 to D-3 as prayed for?

iv. To what relief?
11.
During trial, the plaintiff got himself examined as P.W.1 and P.W.2 was also examined and Exs.A-1 to A-6 were marked on behalf of the plaintiff.
Defendant No.1 got himself examined as D.W.1 and D.W.2 was also examined and Exs.B-1 to B-4 were marked on behalf of defendants.
The appellate Court marked Exs.A-7 to A-10 on behalf of the plaintiff.

12. On a consideration of the evidence available on record, the trial Court held that the plaintiff miserably failed to establish that defendant No.1 with the help of defendant No.2 obtained Ex.A-1 sale deed under coercion by using force and as such he is not entitled to seek for cancellation of Ex.A-1 sale deed and, accordingly,
dismissed the suit.

13. Aggrieved by the judgment and decree of the trial Court, the plaintiff filed A.S.No.61 of 2010 assailing the findings of the trial Court on the ground that the trial Court failed to appreciate the evidence produced by them and came to the wrong conclusion and prayed to set aside the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court in O.S.No.93 of 2009.

14. The learned Additional District Judge framed the following point for consideration:
"Whether the suit of the plaintiff can be decreed by setting aside the judgment of the lower Court?

15. On reappraisal of the evidence on record, the appellate Court held that when defendant No.1 started construction on the suit plot, it is nothing but illegal for the reason that under coercion, he got executed the sale deed from the plaintiff and as such his possession over the suit plot is not lawful and defendant No.1 can be restrained by way of interim injunction from interfering with the possession of the T. sentences.text: Accordingly, the appeal was allowed with costs of Rs.20,000/- and the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court was set aside.

The appellate Court also imposed costs of Rs.25,000/- on defendant No.2.
16. S.A.No.1422 of 2011 was admitted on the following substantial questions of law:
i.

Whether the judgment of the first appellate Court is not vitiated for not framing (a)
the points for determination (b) the decision thereon (c) the reasons for the decision as required under O. 41. R. 31 of the C.P.C.
 ii. Whether the judgment of the first appellate court is  not vitiated for not framing the point for determination as to whether the impugned sale deed is vitiated by coercion and undue influence and for not giving a finding as to how the plaintiff has established that he was illegally confined in police station from 9.1.2007 to 12.1.2007 during which period he was allegedly coerced and threatened to execute the impugned sale deed dated 12.1.2007 (Ex. A-1) & how he was forced to register it.

iii. Whether the judgment of the first appellate court is not vitiated for entering into a discussion as to whether the sale consideration mentioned in the sale deed dated 12.1.2007 (Ex. A-1) was paid or not and then giving a finding in the absence of any finding or grievance made by the plaintiff in his plaint or issue being framed.
The first appellate court failed to see that the plaint case is that the execution of sale deed is vitiated by coercion and not for non-payment of sale consideration.
iv. Whether judgment of the first appellate court is not vitiated for giving a relief that is neither pleaded nor prayed for.

v. Whether the findings of the first appellate court regarding possession of the first defendant are not vitiated in the absence of any averments in the plaint or prayer in the plaint and without any issue and then proceeding to grant injunction without a pleading or prayer in the plaint.

vi. Whether the finding of the first appellate court regarding the nature of construction raised is valid without an issue being framed and without examining the relevancy of the same to the relief prayed for in the suit?

vii. Whether the imposition of exemplary costs of Rs.20,000/- is justified without a plea or prayer as against defendant No.1 and without an issue nor framing a point for determination nor giving reasons therefor?

viii. The first appellate court was not justified in imposing exemplary costs of Rs.
20,000/- and costs of Rs. 34,249/-.
The same are liable to be set aside.

18. Sri M.Jagannatha Sarma, learned counsel for the appellant in S.A.No.1422 of 2011 vehemently contended that the appellate Court has not followed the provisions of order XLI Rule 31 CPC and framed only one point for determination and said the findings are perverse and against facts and law.
Learned counsel further submitted that the judgment of the appellate Court is vitiated for not framing the points for determination as mandated under Order XLI Rule 31 CPC.
He has submitted that the appellate Court granted relief as prayed and also granted the relief of perpetual injunction without any averment or claim being made in the plaint.

The judgment and decree of the appellate Court is liable to be set aside and without there being any proper appreciation of the evidence on record and not considering the grounds of appeal before the appellate Court, the reversal judgment and decree of the trial Court is not sustainable.

In support of his submissions and contentions, learned counsel for the appellant relied on the decisions reported in H.SIDDIQUI v. A.RAMALINGAM1,
RAHEEM v. KARNATAKA ELECTRICITY BOARD2 and RAVINDER SINGH v.
JANMEJA SINGH AND OTHERS3.

The said finding is perverse and contrary to the evidence on record.

The appellate Court has wrongly appreciated the evidence that respondent No.1 was confined in police station and he was coerced to execute a registered sale deed in favour of respondent No.2 and without there being any proof of such allegation, the said finding is given.

The judgment of the appellate Court is based on inadequate consideration of the evidence on record and the same is contrary to law and facts and liable to be set aside.

On the contrary, Sri Gopala Krishna Kalanidhi, learned counsel for respondent No.1 in both the second appeals has vehemently submitted that both the second appeals are not maintainable and the appellate Court on proper re-appreciation of the entire material in record had rightly gave reversal finding on he judgment and decree of the trial Court.
The appeals lacks merit and are liable to be dismissed.
21. I have considered the rival submissions made by learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

22. The main substantial questions of law is - whether the judgment and decree of the appellate Court is vitiated for not framing (a) the point for determination (b) the decision thereon and (c) the reasons for decision as required.

23. The appellate Court while dealing with the judgment of the trial Court has framed only the following point for determination:
"Whether the suit of the plaintiff can be decreed by setting aside the judgment of the lower Court?

The appellate Court failed to realize that it was deciding the first appeal and that it had to be decided strictly in adherence to the provisions contained in order XLI Rule 31 CPC.
24.

Undisputedly, the appellate Court without framing any points for determination went on recording the reversal findings which are not at all averred or pleaded by the plaintiff and only basing on the relief claimed had granted perpetual injunction restraining defendant No.1 from raising any construction in the suit schedule property.

The said finding was recorded without taking into consideration the fact that the plaintiff in his evidence himself stated that defendant No.1 had already constructed and completed the house and also admitted that the plaintiff continued to remain out of possession of the suit schedule property.
Interestingly, in the plaint schedule, the suit property is described as open plot.

Apart from the above, the appellate Court, without framing a point for determination and without there being any grievance pleaded by the plaintiff, entered into discussion as to whether the sale consideration mentioned in the sale deed dated 12.01.2007 Ex.A-1 was paid or not and rendered a finding and also failed to notice that the averment in the plaint was that the sale deed was vitiated as the same was executed by putting the plaintiff under coercion and not for non-payment of sale consideration.
Therefore, without noticing all these facts, the above finding is recorded contrary to the evidence on record.

25. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Siddiqui's case (1 supra) gave a finding in paragraphs 21 and 22, which is quite relevant to the facts and circumstances of this case whereunder the High Court being the appellate Court has failed to frame appropriate points for determination as mandated under order XLI Rule 31 CPC and T. sentences.text: It is a settled position of law that an appeal is a continuation of the proceedings of the original court.
Ordinarily, the appellate jurisdiction involves a re-hearing on law as well as on fact and is invoked by an aggrieved person.
The first appeal is a valuable right of the appellant and therein all questions of fact and law decided by the trial court are open for re-consideration.
Therefore, the first appellate court is required to address itself to all the issues and decide the case by giving reasons.
The court of first appeal must record its findings only after dealing with all issues of law as well as fact and with the evidence, oral as well as documentary, led by the parties.

The judgment of the first appellate court must display conscious application of mind and record findings supported by reasons on all issues and contentions [see: Santosh Hazari v.
Purushottam Tiwari (Deceased) By Lrs., Madhukar and others v. Sangram and Others,
B.M.Narayana Gowda v. Shanthamma (Dead) By Lrs. And Another, H. K. N. Swami v. Irshad Basith (Dead) By Lrs. and M/s.

Section 100 expressly bars second appeal unless a question of law is involved in a case and the question of law so involved is substantial in nature.

sentences.text: It is settled law that an appeal is a continuation of the original proceedings.
The appellate court's jurisdiction involves a rehearing of appeal on questions of law as well as fact.

The first appeal is a valuable right, and, at that stage,
all questions of fact and law decided by the trial court are open for reconsideration.

The judgment of the appellate court must, therefore, reflect conscious application of mind and must record the court's findings, 5 2022 SCC OnLine SC 736 supported by reasons for its decision in respect of all the issues, along with the contentions put forth and pressed by the parties.
Needless to say, the first appellate court is required to comply with the requirements of Order 41 Rule 31 CPC and non-observance of these requirements lead to infirmity in the judgment.

28. From the above settled legal principles, it is clear that the appellate Court has to set out points for determination, record the decision thereon and give its own reasons while deciding the appeal.
Keeping in mind the said principles, let me examine the instant case.

It is evident in the instant case that the appellate Court had committed a serious error in neither framing the points for determination nor re-appreciating the evidence on record, keeping in view the settled principles of law and facts.

29. A perusal of the reversal judgment and decree of the trial Court, the same is without proper re-appreciation of evidence of the parties and without any proper reasons by framing appropriate points for determination and also failing to follow the provisions of Order XLI Rule 31 CPC while deciding the appeal.

Normally, in the said facts and circumstances, the matter would be required to be remanded to the appellate Court for fresh consideration and disposal of the appeal by following the requirements of Order XLI Rule 31 CPC by framing the points for determination and re-appreciation of oral and documentary evidence of the parties.
30. In view of the above, I am of the considered opinion that the appellate Court had not proceeded to adjudicate upon on the appeal strictly in accordance with law.
I am not inclined to enter into the issue of merits of the parties on appreciation of the oral and documentary evidence, since the judgment cannot be sustained in the eye of the law.

sentences.text: Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the matter is remanded to the appellate Court by setting aside its judgment and decree dated 18.08.2011 in A.S.No.61 of 2010, on the file of the I-Additional District Judge, Karimnagar and requesting the appellate Court to decide the same afresh in accordance with law.

Since the matter is pending for more than one and half decades, the appellate Court shall decide A.S.No.61 of 2010 on merits, duly following the provisions of XLI Rule 31 CPC, as expeditiously as possible, preferably within a period of three months from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
It is clarified that any observation made hereinabove shall not adversely effect the cause of either of the parties.
32. In the result, both the second appeals stand allowed as stated above.
There shall be no order as to costs.
33. Miscellaneous petitions, if any pending, stand closed.

In support of his submissions and contentions, learned counsel for the appellant relied on the decisions reported in H.SIDDIQUI v. A.RAMALINGAM1,
RAHEEM v. KARNATAKA ELECTRICITY BOARD2 and RAVINDER SINGH v.
JANMEJA SINGH AND OTHERS3.
19.
The said finding is perverse and contrary to the evidence on record.
On the contrary, Sri Gopala Krishna Kalanidhi, learned counsel for respondent No.1 in both the second appeals has vehemently submitted that both the second appeals are not maintainable and the appellate Court on proper re-appreciation of the entire material in record had rightly gave reversal finding on he judgment and decree of the trial Court.
The appeals lacks merit and are liable to be dismissed.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
26. In MULLURU MALLAPPA (D) THR. Lrs. v.
KURUVATHAPPA4, the Hon'ble Supreme Court while dealing with the provisions of Section 96 CPC and Order XLI Rule 31 CPC held at paragraphs 14, 15 and 16 as under:
4 (2020) 4 SCC 313 14.
It is a settled position of law that an appeal is a continuation of the proceedings of the original court.
Ordinarily, the appellate jurisdiction involves a re-hearing on law as well as on fact and is invoked by an aggrieved person.
The first appeal is a valuable right of the appellant and therein all questions of fact and law decided by the trial court are open for re-consideration.
Therefore, the first appellate court is required to address itself to all the issues and decide the case by giving reasons.
The court of first appeal must record its findings only after dealing with all issues of law as well as fact and with the evidence, oral as well as documentary, led by the parties.
It is settled law that an appeal is a continuation of the original proceedings.
The appellate court's jurisdiction involves a rehearing of appeal on questions of law as well as fact.
The first appeal is a valuable right, and, at that stage,
all questions of fact and law decided by the trial court are open for reconsideration.
Needless to say, the first appellate court is required to comply with the requirements of Order 41 Rule 31 CPC and non-observance of these requirements lead to infirmity in the judgment.
28. From the above settled legal principles, it is clear that the appellate Court has to set out points for determination, record the decision thereon and give its own reasons while deciding the appeal.
It is evident in the instant case that the appellate Court had committed a serious error in neither framing the points for determination nor re-appreciating the evidence on record, keeping in view the settled principles of law and facts.
29. A perusal of the reversal judgment and decree of the trial Court, the same is without proper re-appreciation of evidence of the parties and without any proper reasons by framing appropriate points for determination and also failing to follow the provisions of Order XLI Rule 31 CPC while deciding the appeal.
Normally, in the said facts and circumstances, the matter would be required to be remanded to the appellate Court for fresh consideration and disposal of the appeal by following the requirements of Order XLI Rule 31 CPC by framing the points for determination and re-appreciation of oral and documentary evidence of the parties.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the matter is remanded to the appellate Court by setting aside its judgment and decree dated 18.08.2011 in A.S.No.61 of 2010, on the file of the I-Additional District Judge, Karimnagar and requesting the appellate Court to decide the same afresh in accordance with law.
Since the matter is pending for more than one and half decades, the appellate Court shall decide A.S.No.61 of 2010 on merits, duly following the provisions of XLI Rule 31 CPC, as expeditiously as possible, preferably within a period of three months from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
It is clarified that any observation made hereinabove shall not adversely effect the cause of either of the parties.
32. In the result, both the second appeals stand allowed as stated above.
There shall be no order as to costs.
33. Miscellaneous petitions, if any pending, stand closed.
